case_title: A 7-year-old whose labs were read with adult ranges
case_summary_for_demo: 7-year-old boy with headaches, thirst, night-time urination and slowing growth. The urgent care lab printed adult reference ranges, so some results looked normal when they may not be for his age.
main_concern: Theo has had headaches most mornings for two weeks, he's always thirsty and he has started wetting the bed again. Urgent care said his labs were fine, but he's one of the shortest in his class now and he isn't himself.

symptoms.symptom: Very thirsty, drinking a lot of water
Waking at night to urinate; bedwetting again
symptoms.details: Had been dry at night since age 4.
Shoe and clothing sizes barely changed in a year.

medications.name: Ibuprofen (children's)
medications.how_often: every 6-8 hours when he has a headache, about once a day

past_history: Three urinary tract infections with fever before age 3 (two emergency visits)
A kidney ultrasound was recommended in 2022 but never done after we moved
family_history: Paternal grandfather: kidney problems (on dialysis in his 60s)

lifestyle.exercise: used to play soccer; less active lately

questions_for_panel: Urgent care said his labs were normal. Are they normal for a 7-year-old?
Why is he so thirsty and wetting the bed?
Should we be worried about his growth?
